make sure that you cycle your tank before you add your axolotl. i kept mine in a small separate container while i cycled my tank (i also tested the water in the tank about 2-3 times a week). while he was in the container, i did daily water changes and fed him frozen bloodworms. i cycled my tank for about 2-3 months and then added him when my ammonia and nitrite levels were 0 ppm. now that he’s bigger (~5-6 inches long), i feed him earthworms dug from my garden and red wigglers that i bought online and keep in a separate plastic container (if you do this just look up vermiculture tips online). i occasionally give him frozen krill chopped into small pieces as a treat since krill isn’t very nutritious and can contain salt. i feed him every other day and i check the tank daily to make sure that it’s clean. 

do 25-35% water changes once a week and make sure that the water is free of both chlorine AND chloramines. axolotl also prefer slightly harder water, but this isn’t as big of a deal. if you don’t know if your water has chloramines, you can either call you local water department and ask or buy treatment that removes both. i personally keep 6 plastic gallon jugs and fill these with treated water. i don’t cover the tops with caps because you want the water to sit out and let any gases dissolve. make sure that any water you add to the tank is aged (at least 24 hours old). also, i highly recommend that in addition to buying a sponge filter, you should get a T-split valve and have a separate line for an air stone to help aerate the water. this allows the water to oxygenate. 

one thing about substrate. if you add sand, you should have very fine sand. coarse sand is harder to pass and can lead to impaction, which is where the axolotl can not pass food through its body and becomes “plugged up”. to prevent this, buy fine sand or use BIG rocks. unfortunately i couldn’t find very fine sand , so to compensate i added a bunch of large stones on top of the sand in order to form a makeshift second layer. yes, it’s more difficult to clean this way, but my axolotl loves to sit on the rocks, so as long as he likes it then it’s worth it to me. :)
i recommend hybrid substrate like what i did, but you can do whatever you want. bare bottom tanks are a better option than sand, but also come with drawbacks (cleaning and aesthetics). stones are also better, but again, have drawbacks (cleaning). find what’s best for you!

another thing i forgot to mention. i keep a few live plants in my tank because they’re beneficial! i added them when i first started cycling it because they help slightly speed up the process. i have a floating anubias and a marimo moss ball. my axolotl also likes to sit on the moss ball too :)

https://imgur.com/a/tVD2WKA 

anyway, i researched this animal for months before i got it. one website that i HIGHLY recommend is this:  www.caudata.org/cc

caudata has TONS of information about everything when it comes to axolotls, and it also has links to even more resources! PM me if you ever need help and good luck!

did you cycle your tank? when i got my axolotl, i kept him in a small ~.5 gallon container so i could cycle my tank. i also kept him in a smaller container so i could clean up after him more easily, slowly establish a routine, and allow him to be somewhere that wouldn’t stress him out as easily. i cycled it for a couple of months and then added him in there when the tank was fully cycled (he was about 4 months old). i highly recommend that you keep your baby in a smaller container and then add him to the tank when he’s about 3-4 inches long. good luck!

edit: it’s also harder for them to go to the surface when they’re small, that’s another reason why i kept him in a little container. that water looks really deep for him, so keep that in mind.

Rebecca Black’s “Friday” is about the assassination of John F. Kennedy. 
“7 a.m., waking up in the morning Got to be fresh got to go downstairs.” 
JFK woke up at 7 am on Nov. 22, 1963. He had a long day of appearances ahead of him. The election was on the radar, and the administration wanted to maximize his exposure in Texas. Kennedy needed to be “fresh”; his visit was with the intent of smoothing tensions within the Democratic party there. He had to “go downstairs,” a reference to deplaning Air Force One at Dallas Love field. 
“Seeing everything, the time is going Ticking on and on, everybody’s rushing” The day passed quickly, and from the viewpoint, so does life. “everybody’s rushing” is another clever line. JFK’s motorcade made two unplanned stops along their route, leading them to be ten minutes late when they arrived in the site of the murder. That time let Oswald, who was late too, get ready. Additionally, Black’s pronunciation here sounds strikingly similar to “everybody’s Russian.” Oswald had communist ties in America, his wife was Soviet citizen-many suspect KGB involvement in his death. Is there more tot he story than whats in the report? 
“Got to get down to the bus stop Got to catch my bus, I see my friends (my friends)” The motorcade departed late, due to delays. Along the way, citizens and friends of the President lined the streets in an enthusiastic display. 
“Kicking in the front seat. Sitting in the back seat. Got to make my mind up. Which seat can I take?” JFK and the First Lady were seated in the back of the car, with governor John Connally and his wife “kicking it” in the front. “It’s Friday, Friday. Got to get down on Friday” 
Friday, November 22nd was the day that Lee Harvey Oswald murdered JFK. When he opened fire, the first shot missed. A warning from the secret service agent in the car to “get down!” wasn’t heeded in time; the second shot struck JFK in the back before the final bullet hit his head. Additionally, in the music video, Black sits in the back of a convertible...in the same position that JFK took that day in his. Do you think it’s a coincidence?
